new_note: *He is grievous to us even to behold: for his life is not like other men’s, his ways are of another fashion.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:15). *The Son of Adam came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.* (Matthew 11:19). The ungodly in Wisdom cannot even stand to look at the righteous man, because his life is cut to another pattern than theirs. That is the complaint behind the slander in Matthew: the Son of Adam sat at table with publicans and sinners, and the religious system of his day could only read a life of another fashion as gluttony and drunkenness. The charge changes its words from one age to the next, but it is the same offense — a righteous life reproves the ones watching it, and they answer by calling it unrighteous. Wisdom is justified of her children all the same.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:15 — *his life is not like other men’s, his ways are of another fashion.* The life of another fashion is what the slander of Matthew 11:19 was aimed at — a glutton and winebibber for sitting with sinners.

new_note: *We are esteemed of him as counterfeits: he abstaineth from our ways as from filthiness: he pronounceth the end of the just to be blessed, and makes his boast that Yahuah (God) is his father.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:16). *And saith unto him, If thou be the Son of Elohim (God), cast thyself down: for it is written, He shall give his angels charge concerning thee: and in their hands they shall bear thee up, lest at any time thou dash thy foot against a stone.* (Matthew 4:6). The ungodly resent one thing above the rest: the righteous man makes his boast that Yahuah (God) is his father. In the wilderness the tempter picks up the same grievance and turns it into a dare — if you are the Son of Elohim (God), prove it, throw yourself down and let the angels catch you. The claim of sonship is treated as something to be tested by a display of rescue. Yahusha (Jesus) did not take the dare, because sonship is shown by doing the Father's will, not by forcing the Father's hand.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:16 — *makes his boast that Yahuah (God) is his father.* The boast the ungodly resent is the claim the tempter dares him to prove at Matthew 4:6.

new_note: *We are esteemed of him as counterfeits: he abstaineth from our ways as from filthiness: he pronounceth the end of the just to be blessed, and makes his boast that Yahuah (God) is his father.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:16). *From that time forth began Yahusha (Jesus) to shew unto his disciples, how that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day.* (Matthew 16:21). The men who esteemed themselves righteous felt judged by a man who would not walk their way and who called Yahuah (God) his father. Wisdom puts the grievance in their own mouths; Matthew names who held it in Yahusha's (Jesus') day — the elders, the chief priests and the scribes, the men who held the seats of religion in Jerusalem. He told his disciples plainly that he must suffer at their hands and be killed, because a life that counts their ways as filthiness is an indictment they could not leave standing. It was the seat of the system that rose against him, not the people sitting under it.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:16 — *We are esteemed of him as counterfeits: he abstaineth from our ways as from filthiness.* The grievance of the religious seat, which is why he must suffer of the elders and chief priests and scribes (Matthew 16:21).

new_note: *We are esteemed of him as counterfeits: he abstaineth from our ways as from filthiness: he pronounceth the end of the just to be blessed, and makes his boast that Yahuah (God) is his father.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:16). *Pilate saith unto him, What is truth? And when he had said this, he went out again unto the Yahudim (Jews), and saith unto them, I find in him no fault at all.* (John 18:38). Pilate looked for a crime and found none. The men pressing for his death had no crime to show either, only what Wisdom had already named: a man whose life rebuked theirs and who made his boast that Yahuah (God) was his father. That was the whole charge — he claimed the Father as his own, and his righteousness made their religion look like counterfeit. The fault the ungodly find in the just is never a crime; it is the reproof they feel just by standing near him.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:16 — *he pronounceth the end of the just to be blessed, and makes his boast that Yahuah (God) is his father.* Pilate found no fault at all (John 18:38); the only charge was the one Wisdom named.

new_note: *For if the just man be the son of Yahuah (God), he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:18). *And saith unto him, If thou be the Son of Elohim (God), cast thyself down: for it is written, He shall give his angels charge concerning thee: and in their hands they shall bear thee up, lest at any time thou dash thy foot against a stone.* (Matthew 4:6). Wisdom puts the test in the mouths of the ungodly: if he really is the son of Yahuah (God), then his Father will have to rescue him. The devil carries the same test into the wilderness almost word for word — if thou be the Son of Elohim (God), cast thyself down, and let the angels bear thee up. He even cuts a line out of Psalm 91 to make the dare sound like scripture. The writer of Wisdom had heard this voice centuries before; the gospel shows whose voice it is.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:18 — *if the just man be the son of Yahuah (God), he will help him.* The ungodly's test is the devil's dare at Matthew 4:6, down to the cut quotation of Psalm 91.

new_note: *For if the just man be the son of Yahuah (God), he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:18). *That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet, saying, Himself took our infirmities, and bare our sicknesses.* (Matthew 8:17). The ungodly think the Father's help for his son would look like rescue from the hand of his enemies. Matthew shows what the help actually looked like: the son himself took our infirmities and bore our sicknesses, as Isaiah said he would. The just man who is the son of Yahuah (God) was not spared the suffering; he carried it, and carried it all through his ministry, not only on the last day. Deliverance came, but it came through the bearing and not around it.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:18 — *he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies.* The help came as bearing, not escape — *Himself took our infirmities, and bare our sicknesses* (Matthew 8:17).
flag: Connection is thin (Wisdom's test of sonship against Matthew's Isaiah quotation); kept the old note's point that the bearing ran through the whole ministry and did not overstate it.

new_note: *For if the just man be the son of Yahuah (God), he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:18). *For whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.* (Matthew 12:50). The ungodly have a test for who is the son of Yahuah (God): will the Father step in and deliver him? Yahusha (Jesus) gives the Father's own test for who belongs to his family: whoever does the will of my Father in heaven. One measures sonship by rescue, the other by obedience. Wisdom shows the just man already living by the second standard before the first is ever applied to him, and that is exactly why his life was grievous to them.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:18 — *For if the just man be the son of Yahuah (God), he will help him.* The ungodly test sonship by rescue; Yahusha (Jesus) marks his family by doing the Father's will (Matthew 12:50).

new_note: *For if the just man be the son of Yahuah (God), he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:18). *And Simon Peter answered and said, Thou art the Messiah (Christ), the Son of the living Elohim (God).* (Matthew 16:16). The same words come from two mouths. The ungodly in Wisdom say it in mockery — if the just man is the son of Yahuah (God), let him be delivered. Peter says it in confession — thou art the Messiah (Christ), the Son of the living Elohim (God). What the wicked used as a taunt against the righteous man is the title the Father reveals to Peter at the turning point of the gospel. The just man of Wisdom is the Son Peter confessed, and the plot to test him never changed who he was.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:18 — *if the just man be the son of Yahuah (God), he will help him.* Said in mockery here; confessed by Peter at Matthew 16:16 as *the Son of the living Elohim (God).*
flag: Old note reached into the nature-of-God question (Formed and Formless against Trinity and its denial); the card does not need it, so the rebuilt note keeps to the taunt-and-confession connection and asserts no doctrine either way.

new_note: *For if the just man be the son of Yahuah (God), he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:18). *When Yahusha (Jesus) therefore had received the vinegar, he said, It is finished: and he bowed his head, and gave up the ghost.* (John 19:30). The ungodly set the terms: if he is the son, his Father will pull him out of their hands. On the cross the terms were met in a way they never imagined. Yahusha (Jesus) did not come down; he finished the work and gave up the ghost. The deliverance came on the third day, not by escape but by resurrection — exactly where Wisdom goes next, when the chapter turns: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1).
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:18 — *he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies.* The deliverance came through *It is finished* (John 19:30) and the third day, not by coming down from the cross.

new_note: *Let us examine him with despitefulness and torture, that we may know his meekness, and prove his patience.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:19). *And when he would have put him to death, he feared the multitude, because they counted him as a prophet.* (Matthew 14:5). Wisdom shows the heart of the ungodly toward the righteous: torment him and see how long his meekness holds. Herod carried that heart toward John; he would have put him to death already, and only his fear of the crowd held his hand. The restraint was politics, not mercy, and a birthday oath later removed it. Isaiah's sheep dumb before her shearers, John in Herod's prison, Yahusha (Jesus) before Pilate — the ungodly keep running the same test on the righteous, and the righteous keep answering it the same way.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:19 — *Let us examine him with despitefulness and torture, that we may know his meekness.* Herod's heart toward John, held back only by fear of the multitude (Matthew 14:5).

new_note: *Let us examine him with despitefulness and torture, that we may know his meekness, and prove his patience.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:19). *Then came Yahusha (Jesus) forth, wearing the crown of thorns, and the purple robe. And Pilate saith unto them, Behold the man!* (John 19:5). Here is the program the ungodly lay out: despitefulness and torture, to see what the righteous man's meekness and patience are made of. John 19 shows it carried out to the letter — Pilate scourged him, the soldiers wove him a crown of thorns and dressed him in purple and struck him, and then he was led out before the crowd. Behold the man. He came forth meek and patient under the very test Wisdom said the ungodly would devise, and the test proved what they refused to see.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:19 — *that we may know his meekness, and prove his patience.* The scourging and the crown of thorns at John 19:1–5 are this test carried out, and *Behold the man* is the answer.

new_note: *Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:20). *Then the devil leaveth him, and, behold, angels came and ministered unto him.* (Matthew 4:11). The plot against the righteous man in Wisdom ends in a death sentence; the plot against Yahusha (Jesus) in the wilderness ends with the devil leaving and angels ministering to him. The two are not in conflict. The wilderness was the opening move, not the last one — the enemy withdrew to come back through other hands. Wisdom names the whole arc from reproof to shameful death; Matthew 4 is where that arc begins in the gospel, and it does not end until the cross.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:20 — *Let us condemn him with a shameful death.* The plot's end; Matthew 4:11's *Then the devil leaveth him* is only the end of its first round.

new_note: *Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:20). *The Son of Adam came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.* (Matthew 11:19). The ungodly in Wisdom finish where they were always headed: condemn him to a shameful death. In Matthew 11 they are only at the beginning — calling him a glutton and a winebibber for sitting with sinners. The road runs from there to Matthew 12, where his works are credited to Beelzebub, and on to the trial and the cross in Matthew 26 and 27. A system that cannot deny what it sees moves from slander to false accusation to execution. Wisdom had named the end of that road before the gospel showed its first step.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:20 — *Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.* The end of the road whose first step is the slander of Matthew 11:19.

new_note: *Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:20). *And he sent, and beheaded John in the prison.* (Matthew 14:10). A shameful death is not the honored end of a long life; it is a death arranged by men who want the righteous man gone. John's beheading in Herod's prison, on the strength of a rash birthday oath, is exactly the death Wisdom describes. The ungodly did not wait for the Father's verdict on his words; they gave their own. The prophets who upbraided the nation with the Torah died this way before him, and the King tells that whole history over in Matthew 23.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:20 — *Let us condemn him with a shameful death.* John beheaded in the prison on a birthday oath (Matthew 14:10) is the death Wisdom describes.

new_note: *Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:20). *From that time forth began Yahusha (Jesus) to shew unto his disciples, how that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day.* (Matthew 16:21). Wisdom says the ungodly will condemn the righteous man to a shameful death. Yahusha (Jesus) tells his disciples he must suffer and be killed, and later he names how: delivered to be mocked, scourged and crucified (Matthew 20:19). The cross was the shameful death — the Torah itself says *he that is hanged is accursed of Elohim (God)* (Deuteronomy 21:23), so the men who hung him there meant it as the Father's own rejection of him. Isaiah's servant, Wisdom's just man and the passion the King announced all meet at that tree. And he named the third day in the same breath, which is the answer to the whole plot.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:20 — *Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.* The shameful death is the cross Yahusha (Jesus) said he must die at Matthew 16:21, hung on the tree of Deuteronomy 21:23.
flag: Old note stacked Galatians 3:13 onto this card; I left it off rather than open the curse-of-the-law question in a four-sentence note. Deuteronomy 21:23 carries the shameful-death point on its own.

new_note: *Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:20). *Ought not Messiah (Christ) to have suffered these things, and to enter into his glory?* (Luke 24:26). On the road to Emmaus Yahusha (Jesus) asked the slow of heart why they were surprised. Ought not Messiah (Christ) to have suffered? The suffering was written — in Moses, in the prophets, and here in Wisdom, where the just man who calls Yahuah (God) his father is sentenced to a shameful death by the men who lay in wait for him. The disciples had read the glory and skipped the suffering. The whole library had both halves on the page, and the King opened their eyes to read them together.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:20 — *Let us condemn him with a shameful death.* The suffering half the Emmaus disciples could not read — *Ought not Messiah (Christ) to have suffered these things* (Luke 24:26).

new_note: *Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:20). *When the chief priests therefore and officers saw him, they cried out, saying, Crucify him, crucify him. Pilate saith unto them, Take ye him, and crucify him: for I find no fault in him.* (John 19:6). Wisdom gives the resolve; John gives the shout. Let us condemn him with a shameful death becomes Crucify him, crucify him in the mouths of the chief priests and officers. Pilate found no fault in him, and still the death was demanded — not for any crime, but because he called Yahuah (God) his father and his life exposed theirs. The crucifixion is the shameful death Wisdom said the ungodly would lay on the just man.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:20 — *Let us condemn him with a shameful death.* The resolve that became *Crucify him, crucify him* at John 19:6.

new_note: *For Yahuah (God) created man to be immortal, and made him to be an image of his own eternity.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:23). *And he saith unto them, Whose is this image and superscription?* (Matthew 22:20). Yahusha (Jesus) asked whose image was on the coin, and the answer settled where the coin belonged. Wisdom tells us whose image is on the man: Yahuah (God) made him an image of his own eternity. Caesar's stamp is on the money, so the money goes back to Caesar; the Father's stamp is on the one holding it, so the one holding it goes back to the Father. The coin is perishable and so is its owner. The man was made for immortality, and the image he bears tells him whose he is.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:23 — *made him to be an image of his own eternity.* Caesar's image is on the coin (Matthew 22:20); the Father's image is on the man who holds it.

new_note: *Nevertheless through envy of the devil came death into the world: and they that do hold of his side do find it.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:24). *The enemy that sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the end of the world; and the reapers are the angels.* (Matthew 13:39). Wisdom names where death came from — the envy of the devil — and who finds it: they that hold of his side. Yahusha (Jesus) names the same enemy as the one who sowed the tares in the field, and in the verse before he calls the tares the children of the wicked one. The serpent in the garden, the watchers who corrupted the earth, the sower of tares in the field — it is one enemy doing one work across the whole story. Those who are of his side come to his end, because the seed shows at the harvest.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:24 — *through envy of the devil came death into the world: and they that do hold of his side.* The enemy who sowed the tares (Matthew 13:39) is the one whose envy let death in.

new_note: *Nevertheless through envy of the devil came death into the world: and they that do hold of his side do find it.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:24). *And he said unto them, I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven.* (Luke 10:18). The one whose envy let death into the world is the one Yahusha (Jesus) saw fall like lightning. When the seventy came back rejoicing that the devils were subject to them, he told them what they had been watching: the enemy who brought death in was being thrown down, and in the next verse he gives them power to tread on serpents and scorpions and over all the power of the enemy. Wisdom names the door death came through; Luke shows the one who opened it losing his footing.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:24 — *through envy of the devil came death into the world.* The one who let death in is the one Yahusha (Jesus) saw fall like lightning (Luke 10:18).

new_note: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1). *Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness’ sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.* (Matthew 5:10). Wisdom's third chapter answers its second. The ungodly tortured and condemned the righteous, and here is where the righteous ended up: in the hand of Yahuah (God), where no torment can reach them. Yahusha (Jesus) says the same to those persecuted for righteousness' sake — the kingdom is theirs. The persecution lands on the body and goes no further. What Wisdom promised the just man, the King promised everyone who would be hated for walking as he walked.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:1 — *the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.* Where the persecuted of Matthew 5:10 end up — theirs is the kingdom.

new_note: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1). *And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.* (Matthew 10:28). Men can kill the body. Wisdom says what they cannot touch: the souls of the righteous, which are in the hand of Yahuah (God). Yahusha (Jesus) tells his disciples the same thing before sending them out among wolves — do not fear the ones who can kill the body but cannot kill the soul. The persecutor's reach stops where the Father's hand begins. The righteous who died under the ungodly in Wisdom 2 were not lost; they were kept.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:1 — *there shall no torment touch them.* The persecutor kills the body but cannot kill the soul held in the Father's hand (Matthew 10:28).

new_note: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1). *From that time forth began Yahusha (Jesus) to shew unto his disciples, how that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day.* (Matthew 16:21). Wisdom 2 ends with the just man condemned to a shameful death; Wisdom 3 opens with his soul in the hand of Yahuah (God), untouched by torment. Yahusha (Jesus) tells his disciples both halves in one sentence — he must be killed, and be raised again the third day. The being killed is the shameful death; the being raised is the hand of the Father. Wisdom had already laid the two chapters side by side, and the gospel shows the one man who walked through both.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:1 — *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God).* The other half of the shameful death — killed, *and be raised again the third day* (Matthew 16:21).

new_note: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1). *But Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said, Ye know not what ye ask. Are ye able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of, and to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with? They say unto him, We are able.* (Matthew 20:22). James and John asked for thrones and were handed a cup. Yahusha (Jesus) asked whether they could drink what he was about to drink, and they said they could, not knowing what they were agreeing to. James was put to the sword by Herod (Acts 12:2); John outlived them all and was on Patmos for the testimony. The cup was real suffering, and Wisdom tells where it ends: the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there no torment touches them. James drank the cup to the bottom and lies down in that hand, kept and asleep until the Father raises him; the sword reached his body and could not follow him there.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:1 — *the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God).* What held the sons of Zebedee while they drank the cup they said they could drink (Matthew 20:22).
flag: Old note framed the King's cup as the Tanakh cup of wrath poured out at a substitutionary level; that is more than the card needs and more than the two verses say, so I kept the cup as the suffering the sons of Zebedee shared and the Father's hand that held them.

new_note: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1). *I am the Elohim (God) of Abraham, and the Elohim (God) of Isaac, and the Elohim (God) of Jacob? Elohim (God) is not the Elohim (God) of the dead, but of the living.* (Matthew 22:32). Read this verse with the rest of its chapter and it is not souls flying off to heaven. The righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God) — kept, at rest, waiting; a few verses on, *in the time of their visitation they shall shine* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:7), and that visitation has not come yet. Yahusha (Jesus) says the same of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob: Elohim (God) is not the Elohim (God) of the dead but of the living. The fathers are asleep and held, and the Father counts them living because he is going to raise them. That is why Paul can tell the grieving not to sorrow as those who have no hope (1 Thessalonians 4:13), and it is the only reason.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:1 — *the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.* Kept and asleep, not in heaven now — the living Abraham, Isaac and Jacob of Matthew 22:32, held for the resurrection.

new_note: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1). *He is not the Elohim (God) of the dead, but the Elohim (God) of the living: ye therefore do greatly err.* (Mark 12:27). The Sadducees denied the resurrection, and Yahusha (Jesus) answered them from the bush: Elohim (God) named himself the Elohim (God) of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob long after they were buried, and he is not the Elohim (God) of the dead. Wisdom explains how the fathers can be counted living while they lie in the ground — their souls are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and no torment touches them there. They rest, held against the day he raises them. To deny that is to err greatly, as he told the Sadducees to their faces.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:1 — *the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God).* Why the fathers are living to the Father — *He is not the Elohim (God) of the dead, but the Elohim (God) of the living* (Mark 12:27).

new_note: *For though they be punished in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:4). *And as touching the dead, that they rise: have ye not read in the book of Moses, how in the bush Elohim (God) spake unto him, saying, I am the Elohim (God) of Abraham, and the Elohim (God) of Isaac, and the Elohim (God) of Jacob?* (Mark 12:26). Wisdom admits the plain fact: the righteous are punished in the sight of men, and men watch them die. Then it names what the watchers cannot see — a hope full of immortality. Yahusha (Jesus) puts the same hope on the record of Moses: at the bush, generations after the patriarchs were buried, Elohim (God) still called himself the Elohim (God) of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Their death was in the sight of men; their life is in his sight. The resurrection is the shape that hope takes when it is kept.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:4 — *though they be punished in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality.* The hope the bush bears witness to at Mark 12:26 — the Elohim (God) of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, long after their burial.

new_note: *And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded: for Yahuah (God) proved them, and found them worthy for himself.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:5). *And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.* (Matthew 10:22). Wisdom calls the suffering of the righteous a proving: Yahuah (God) chastens a little, tests the metal, and finds them worthy of himself. Yahusha (Jesus) tells his disciples the same thing from the other side — you will be hated of all men for my name's sake, and the one who endures to the end will be saved. The hatred is the furnace; the enduring is what the furnace proves. The reward is great because the trial was real, and the Father is the one who did the proving.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:5 — *Yahuah (God) proved them, and found them worthy for himself.* The proving is the hatred of all men; *he that endureth to the end shall be saved* (Matthew 10:22).

new_note: *As gold in the furnace has he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:6). *For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.* (Ecclesiasticus 2:5). Two wisdom books, one furnace. Sirach says gold is tried in the fire and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity; Wisdom says Yahuah (God) tried the righteous as gold in the furnace and received them as a burnt offering. The fire does not destroy the gold; it shows what the gold is. The righteous who were tormented and killed in Wisdom 2 were being refined, not discarded, and what came through the fire was received at the altar.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:6 — *As gold in the furnace has he tried them.* Sirach says the same at Ecclesiasticus 2:5 — *acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.*

new_note: *And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:7). *Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Who hath ears to hear, let him hear.* (Matthew 13:43). Wisdom puts the shining of the righteous at a set time — the time of their visitation — and sets it in a harvest scene: sparks running among the stubble. Yahusha (Jesus) puts it at the same moment in the parable of the tares: when the field is reaped and the tares are bundled for the fire, then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun. The stubble burning and the sparks flying are the same picture as the tares burning and the wheat shining. The shining is not yet; it waits on the harvest.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:7 — *in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble.* The harvest scene of Matthew 13:43 — tares to the fire, *then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun.*

new_note: *And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:7). *Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing.* (Matthew 24:46). Wisdom sets the shining of the righteous at the time of their visitation — the day the Master comes to look in on his house. Yahusha (Jesus) describes that same day from the servant's side: blessed is that servant whom his lord, when he comes, finds so doing. The visitation is the coming. The servant found at his work when the Master arrives is the one who shines, which is what Daniel saw as well — *they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament* (Daniel 12:3).
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:7 — *in the time of their visitation they shall shine.* The visitation is the lord's coming at Matthew 24:46, and the servant found so doing is the one who shines.

new_note: *And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:7). *When the Son of Adam shall come in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory:* (Matthew 25:31). The time of the righteous' visitation in Wisdom is the day Yahusha (Jesus) describes at the opening of the sheep and the goats: the Son of Adam coming in his glory with all the holy angels, and sitting on the throne of his glory. That is the visitation. The righteous who were killed in the sight of men shine on that day and not before, the way Daniel saw it — *they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament* (Daniel 12:3). The throne and the shining arrive together.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:7 — *in the time of their visitation they shall shine.* The visitation is the Son of Adam coming in his glory at Matthew 25:31.
flag: Old note tied the shining to 1 Thessalonians 4:13–17 as one gathered-and-caught-up event; the author's teaching keeps 4:16 and 4:17 as separate events, so I dropped the 1 Thessalonians line and kept Daniel 12:3.

new_note: *And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:7). *He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where Yahusha (Lord) lay.* (Matthew 28:6). The angel at the tomb announced the first man to pass through Wisdom's time of visitation: He is not here, for he is risen. The righteous who are held in the Father's hand shine when he visits them, and the empty tomb is the firstfruits of that day — *Messiah (Christ) the firstfruits; afterward they that are Messiah's (Christ's) at his coming* (1 Corinthians 15:23). Daniel saw the rest of them still sleeping in the dust until they awake and shine (Daniel 12:2–3). One has risen; the others rest and wait for the same visitation.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:7 — *in the time of their visitation they shall shine.* The empty tomb at Matthew 28:6 is the firstfruits of that visitation; the rest sleep and wait.

new_note: *They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people, and their Elohim (God) shall reign for ever.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:8). *So shall it be at the end of the world: the angels shall come forth, and sever the wicked from among the just,* (Matthew 13:49). Wisdom says the righteous will judge the nations and have dominion over the people. Yahusha (Jesus) says what has to happen first: at the end of the age the angels come and sever the wicked from among the just. The sorting comes before the ruling. Once the wicked are taken out from among them, the just who are left are the ones Wisdom sees judging the nations — a kingdom of priests to the peoples left alive after that day, under an Elohim (God) who reigns for ever.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:8 — *They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people.* After the angels sever the wicked from among the just (Matthew 13:49), the just are the ones who judge.

new_note: *They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people, and their Elohim (God) shall reign for ever.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:8). *And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Adam shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 19:28). Wisdom says the righteous shall judge the nations; Yahusha (Jesus) tells the twelve they shall sit on twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel). These are two views of one kingdom. The gathered twelve tribes sit under the apostles' thrones, and that gathered people is the kingdom of priests the Father promised at Sinai — *ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests* (Exodus 19:6) — who judge and teach the nations left alive in the reign. The priesthood toward the nations begins when the kingdom is set up, not before. Wisdom saw the outer ring; the King named the inner one.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:8 — *They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people.* The outer ring of the kingdom whose inner ring is the twelve thrones over the twelve tribes (Matthew 19:28).

new_note: *They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people, and their Elohim (God) shall reign for ever.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:8). *And before him shall be gathered all nations: and he shall separate them one from another, as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats:* (Matthew 25:32). Before the righteous judge the nations there is a gathering and a sorting. Yahusha (Jesus) says all nations are gathered before him and he separates them as a shepherd divides sheep from goats — the seed brought out of every nation and sifted, the way Ezekiel saw it pass under the rod. Then the sifted remnant, his brethren of Matthew 25:40, does what Wisdom says: judges the nations and has dominion over the people. Daniel saw the same order — *judgment was given to the saints of the El Elyon (most High); and the time came that the saints possessed the kingdom* (Daniel 7:22). The gathering comes first, the reign after.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:8 — *They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people.* The reign that follows the gathering and sorting of Matthew 25:32 — sheep from goats first, then the saints possess the kingdom.

new_note: *They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people, and their Elohim (God) shall reign for ever.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:8). *He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where Yahusha (Lord) lay.* (Matthew 28:6). Wisdom sees the righteous judging the nations and ruling the people under an Elohim (God) who reigns for ever — the reign John saw on the earth, where *they lived and reigned with Messiah (Christ) a thousand years* (Revelation 20:4). That reign needs risen saints, and the empty tomb is where the rising began: He is not here, for he is risen. The first to rise is the one who will seat the rest. This is not souls escaping to heaven while the earth burns; it is the dead raised to rule on the earth with their King, the way Daniel said the saints of the most High would take the kingdom.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:8 — *their Elohim (God) shall reign for ever.* The reign of risen saints on the earth, which began with *he is risen* at Matthew 28:6.

new_note: *They that put their trust in him shall understand the truth: and such as be faithful in love shall abide with him: for grace and mercy is to his saints, and he has care for his elect.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:9). *Rejoice, and be exceeding glad: for great is your reward in heaven: for so persecuted they the prophets which were before you.* (Matthew 5:12). Wisdom closes its word to the persecuted righteous with what they have coming: understanding of the truth, abiding with him, grace and mercy to his saints, and his care over his elect. Yahusha (Jesus) says the same to his disciples — rejoice, for great is your reward in heaven, for so they persecuted the prophets before you. The disciples are being added to the line of the prophets who were hated for speaking the Father's word, and the care and reward Wisdom promised the elect is laid up for them in the same place.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:9 — *grace and mercy is to his saints, and he has care for his elect.* The reward laid up for the persecuted at Matthew 5:12, who join the line of the prophets.

new_note: *And blessed is the eunuch, which with his hands has wrought no iniquity, nor imagined wicked things against Yahuah (God): for to him shall be given the special gift of faith, and an inheritance in the temple of Yahuah (God) more acceptable to his mind.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:14). *For there are some eunuchs, which were so born from their mother’s womb: and there are some eunuchs, which were made eunuchs of men: and there be eunuchs, which have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven’s sake. He that is able to receive it, let him receive it.* (Matthew 19:12). Wisdom blesses the eunuch who has kept his hands clean and promises him the special gift of faith and an inheritance in the house of Yahuah (God). Isaiah had said it first — *even unto them will I give in mine house and within my walls a place and a name better than of sons and of daughters* (Isaiah 56:5). Yahusha (Jesus) speaks of eunuchs who have made themselves so for the kingdom of heaven's sake, and adds: he that is able to receive it, let him receive it. All three treat it as a gift received, not a rule imposed, which is the word both the system that made celibacy a requirement for its clergy and the system that treats the unmarried as half a life managed to miss. The inheritance is for the one to whom it is given.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:14 — *to him shall be given the special gift of faith, and an inheritance in the temple of Yahuah (God).* The gift behind Matthew 19:12's *he that is able to receive it, let him receive it.*

new_note: *For though they flourish in branches for a time; yet standing not last, they shall be shaken with the wind, and through the force of winds they shall be rooted out.* (Wisdom of Solomon 4:4). *And when he saw a fig tree in the way, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only, and said unto it, Let no fruit grow on thee henceforward for ever. And presently the fig tree withered away.* (Matthew 21:19). Wisdom describes the brood of the ungodly as branches that flourish for a while with nothing under them; the wind shakes them and finally roots them out. Yahusha (Jesus) came to a fig tree in full leaf, found no fruit, and it withered. Leaves without fruit is the same picture as branches without roots — a show of life with nothing feeding it. The tree stands for the religious leadership of that day, which had the look of the covenant and none of its fruit; it does not stand for the people of Yashar'el (Israel) as a whole. What flourishes without a root does not stand when the wind comes.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 4:4 — *though they flourish in branches for a time; yet standing not last.* Leaves without fruit at Matthew 21:19 is the same show of life with nothing under it.
